A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOOSE-Chem study and TOMATO-Chem benchmark. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A.1–A.16 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original inspiration-retrieval, hypothesis-generation and ranking experiments, including ablations and expert evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original benchmark experiments, ablations, automatic evaluations and expert assessments.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same inspiration screening, evolutionary mutation/refinement/recombination, multiround beam search and hypothesis scoring. The expanded mathematical treatment does not establish a change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 51 chemistry/materials-science papers and inspiration corpora containing up to 3,000 papers. The additional chemistry and AI examples in Appendix A.1 are conceptual illustrations, not new evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 10, 13 and 14 retain SciMON, MOOSE and Qi et al. (2024). Table 5 retains GPT-4o and the same three Llama-3.1 sizes. Comparator participation is unchanged.

E3.justification: Corpus sizes, screening configurations, the 300-paper end-to-end setting, top-4% inspiration selection, evaluation metrics and expert-selection procedures are unchanged. The expanded appendix does not report revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the window-size, background, evolutionary-unit, multistep and significance-feedback ablations, alternative-evaluator checks, ranking analyses and agreement studies. Appendix A.16 contains the same four cases and expert analyses, with reordered presentation.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added. Tables 19–20 retain the same agreement definitions and 392/48 comparison-pair counts.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and empirical findings match throughout both versions. For example, Table 10 retains MOOSE-Chem's Top MS of 4.020 and Average MS of 2.564. The Claude/Gemini results, expert-score distributions and case-study scores also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 substantially extends the formal argument. Where v4 directly uses a single-path product and states that inspiration order is exchangeable, v5 defines valid permutations, introduces an explicit fixed-constructive-path assumption, and adds marginalization formulas in Equations 12 and 21–22. It also distinguishes the full inspiration knowledge space from its finite corpus approximation. The main-text product formula remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The v5 abstract explicitly calls the three subtasks sufficient, strengthening v4's introductory formulation that they approach sufficient conditions, and characterizes inspiration retrieval as inherently out of distribution. The central rediscovery claim, benchmark contribution and latent-knowledge-association conjecture were already present.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 adds interpretations of clean knowledge elements versus noisy papers, beneficial redundancy across papers, the finite-corpus approximation, and differences in inspiration-order sensitivity between chemistry and mathematics. Existing empirical interpretations and limitations concerning ranking and Matched Score remain.

D1.justification: v5 removes v4's first-page code-and-benchmark availability statement and repository link without providing replacement access information. Existing prompts, annotation instructions and configuration details remain. This establishes removal of access documentation, not unavailability of the resources themselves.

R1.justification: The reference list, Section 2, Appendix A.11 and the comparison with Swanson Linking retain the same cited works and substantive relationships to prior research.

P1.justification: v5 rewrites the abstract, expands Appendix A.1 with structured examples and explanatory prose, makes scattered language and terminology edits, and places ground-truth hypotheses before generated hypotheses in the case studies. The overall section sequence and narrative organization remain.

P2.justification: Figure 2 relabels its corpus input as 'Inspiration Corpus: Lots of Chemistry Papers.' Appendix A.1 adds a state-transition schematic and colored example terms. Appendix tables and figures are regrouped and reflowed, while existing table structures and Figure 1 remain essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves conceptual transparency by making the ordering assumption and finite-corpus approximation explicit and explaining the relationship between inspirations and retrieved papers. These additions help readers assess the existing framework without changing its empirical support. The benefit is limited: the expanded derivation remains assumption-dependent, and removal of the code-and-benchmark link weakens reproducibility guidance.
